_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average index of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices set to 100 in 2015, currently stands at 132, indicating a 32% overall increase since that base year. This rise reflects recent, uneven price movements among the components rather than steady inflation. The index captures global commodity price changes and is useful for tracking cost trends in common breakfast items.
notes.movers: Coffee and orange juice have been the primary drivers, with coffee prices up 93% and orange juice up 22% since 2015. Wheat and sugar showed smaller increases of 7% and 5%, respectively. These shifts stem largely from supply disruptions linked to weather events and crop diseases—for instance, coffee growing regions experiencing frost or drought, and orange juice production affected by hurricanes and citrus greening disease. It is important to note that soft commodities like these trade on relatively thin markets, where such localized factors can cause large price swings.
notes.why: The headline rise in breakfast commodity prices is largely attributable to a few weather-sensitive crops, rather than broad inflationary pressures. Given the nature of these agricultural risks, elevated prices can persist for years until supply conditions improve.
